author: KooDaLord
body:
Well, instead of me going through plenty of maps and commenting about lack of building detail, I decided to make a little post on what makes a map look good, and how to do it.


First of all, making builds look good is all about depth. Depth meaning, make it 3D! Lets say you have a wall, made out of stone brick. First of all, don't just make it pure stone brick, incorporate a coloring/detailing block! First thing to do with this wall is make impressions and depressions, have some part of the wall detail pop out, and some sink in.

Another thing is, when building, unless you are purposely making a map to serve the purpose of being rainbow, then pick a dominant block (best would be drab blocks, like stone brick, cobble, 43:8 and slabs, quartz, wood etc...) and that will be the main block. Build outlines of what you will make, like, have you ever seen real life buildings in the making? They have outlines, like just a bare skeleton of wood. Do that, and then fill it in.

After you have picked your dominant block, also use the slabs and stairs of the same block (like if you are using stone brick, use either cobble or stone brick stairs and slabs). Don't just go to town with them, but they are a huge part of building with depth, and honestly are the most important detailing block. Now, what I like to do is pick a color/popout block or two to use. These blocks can be any color that you would like, but don't mix like purple and lime together, maybe just use 1 colored block, or something like light green clay and dark green clay. This block(s) will be use sparingly. This will be a block that you carefully choose where to place, just make sure that it pops out, and doesn't just turn the whole map that color :P
Now I will show progress of a stone brick and red wall evolve from plain stone brick to an in-depth beautiful wall pattern. (I created all of these stages):
